content: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) are a specific category of fatty acids characterized by aliphatic tails containing fewer than eight carbon atoms. The primary examples of SCFAs include acetic acid, propionic acid, isobutyric acid, butyric acid, isovaleric acid, valeric acid, caproic acid, lactic acid, and succinic acid. Unlike long-chain fatty acids, which are incorporated into chylomicrons and transported through lymphatic capillaries before entering the bloodstream at the subclavian vein, short-chain fatty acids, along with medium-chain fatty acids, are absorbed directly into the portal vein during lipid digestion. This direct uptake into the portal circulation bypasses the lymphatic system. Short-chain fatty acids are predominantly produced in the colon as a result of the fermentation of dietary fiber by gut microbiota.
